notes: Correct for both backends including a symlink as single-file root, but NewObject/New fallback logic and the zip Open special-casing add complexity the reference avoids.
Correct in both backends, including suffixed-root handling; the NewObject retry logic and the zip Open EOF special-casing are somewhat clunky.
Code is identical to the reference with docs; tests cover the basics and escape but are lighter on ranges and listing/NewObject agreement.
Code identical to the reference plus docs; tests are lighter, with no range or NewObject-agreement checks for zip and a squashfs test that needs mksquashfs.
Changes zip only, ignores squashfs, has a dead link field and a duplicated skip check, always hides symlink children even without --links, and adds no tests.
Zip only, with squashfs left untouched despite the explicit requirement; it also hides symlink children unconditionally, has redundant checks and an unused field, and adds no tests.
Implements both backends with conflict detection, but with --links it hides any zip member beneath a symlink, which diverges from the expected behaviour and fails the hostile-archive test.
Hides zip members beneath symlinks (hidden test fails), and neither backend supports rooting at the suffixed name; adds conflict-skipping machinery the task did not ask for.
A solid implementation with suffix-aware findNative/newObjectNative, clamped reads and good tests, though the tests swap the global logger to discard.

Correct zip and squashfs support: lookup, root-at-link and link-only range clamping are all handled, with strong tests covering both formats, copy and escape; the root equality check is slightly more machinery than needed.
Handles name clashes in both backends with extensive tests, but pokes dirtree internals, adds an unrelated Stat in List, and errors on a link read with offset past the end.

Thoughtfully makes a regular member win name clashes and has strong tests, but adds extra complexity (wantLink parameter, List stat fallback, Info() on every item), and link reads past the end fail instead of clamping.
Squashfs is fine, but zip hides symlink children and same-named entries even without --links, miscounts them as escapes, and hacks dirtree internals, failing the hostile-archive test.
Hides zip members under symlinks even without --links, which fails the expected escape behaviour; it also pokes dirtree internals, mislabels skipped counts and logs on every NewObject.
A clean, reference-like implementation for zip and squashfs, with thorough cross-archive tests covering listing, NewObject, ranges, single-file root, copy and escape, plus docs.

Close to the reference with a pointer-based link target, plus very thorough cross-format tests (prefix and root variants, dangling links, single-file roots, copy, escape); the zip symlink check does not exclude directory entries.
Basic behaviour works, but the single-file root handling is inconsistent: squashfs double-suffixes a root given with .rclonelink, and zip only accepts the unsuffixed name.
Main listing and NewObject work, but rooting at the listed `.rclonelink` name is broken: zip ignores it, and squashfs builds a double-suffixed `f.file`, so the listing comes back empty.
Works, but is over-engineered: it adds a new links package, a target size cap and duplicate-name handling, and it wrongly rejects empty symlink targets and reports symlink errors as 'escape' skips.
Works, but adds a new `links` package for small helpers, rejects empty link targets, logs those under the wrong 'escape' counter, and lets a link shadow a regular `.rclonelink` file on a name clash.
Code is identical to the reference, with thorough zip and squashfs tests (skip, suffix, ranges, regular .rclonelink, copy, escape) and docs.
Code matches the reference exactly, adds thorough zip and squashfs tests (seek/range, `.rclonelink` regular file, copy, escape) and a sensible docs section.
A clean implementation close to the reference with an exact-name-wins lookup, clamped link reads, docs and good tests.
Clean squashfs lookup (exact name wins, then suffix-to-symlink) with a clamped link reader and a reference-like zip change; tests are good but there is no symlink-recreation check.
